messages:
jordan: Customer reported a sudden break after upgrading @redwood/node-sdk from v1.3.2 -> v1.4.0. Calls that used to work now return either 404 or 400.

jordan: Quote from their logs: `HTTP 404 Route not found: /v1/chat/completions` and sometimes `400 unexpected field \"messages\"` for the same payload. They say pinning back to v1.3.2 fixes it.

jordan: Repro steps they gave:
```
# typescript
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'redwood-1.2',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
})
```

kevin: Thanks — tagging sdk team. Do we have any intentional endpoint rename in 1.4.0? I don’t see changes in release notes that would remove `/v1/chat/completions`.

sara: Can you paste the full HTTP response (body + headers)? need to check x-redwood-version/x-sdk-version/route hints.

jordan: Full response body (copied):
```
{ "error": { "message": "unexpected field: messages", "type": "invalid_request", "param": "messages" } }
```
Headers include `x-redwood-runtime: hosted`, `x-request-id: req_abc123`, `x-sdk-version: @redwood/node@1.4.0`

kevin: Hmm — looks like the server is expecting the older param name `conversation` (or a different shape) while the SDK is sending `messages`. That suggests a mismatch between the runtime API shape and the published SDK bindings. Possibly a model-serving rollout landed that advertises a different contract.

matt: I can try to repro locally with a pinned env. Jordan, do you have the exact request payload and the request-id from the failing call? I'll search logs with that x-request-id.

jordan: Provided `x-request-id: req_abc123` above. Payload same as the code block. Customer also noted that non-chat endpoints (embeddings/generate) are fine. Only chat surfaces this.

kevin: Quick triage: 1) Confirmed bug in our internal integration test where client.chat was wired to new backend path `/v1/conversations/complete` but our router still exposes `/v1/chat/completions` for older runtime. 2) Accidentally bumped default shape in SDK PR #842 without a compatibility shim.

alice: Immediate mitigation suggestions? Customer is blocked in production.

kevin: Short-term: ask them to pin to `@redwood/node@1.3.2` (npm i @redwood/node@1.3.2). That restores old behavior. Medium-term: we will publish 1.4.1 that provides a compat flag.

sara: Can we also add a server-side fallback so 1.4.0 clients aren’t broken? If router can accept both `messages` and `conversation` shapes we can avoid more escalations.

matt: Opened an SRE ticket to add a permissive parsing fallback on gateway for chat routes — linking: https://internal/tickets/RED-8472. SRE will patch today.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: redwood-gateway patch (fallback parser) -> staging -> prod (canary). ETA ~2h.

kevin: For the support reply: ask customer to pin to 1.3.2 for now, include a short repro and the request-id. We'll follow up once gateway patch is live or SDK 1.4.1 is published.

jordan: Sent customer workaround. They asked if retries would help — they said sometimes they get 404 intermittent.

kevin: Intermittent 404s probably due to mixed runtime versions behind the gateway during rollout. Retries might help but not reliable. Better to pin SDK or wait for gateway patch.

alice: Adding assignment: kevin to cut 1.4.1 with compat flag; matt to confirm rollout and SRE ticket. Jordan to follow up with customer and confirm repro after patch.

kevin: I'll branch a quick fix: revert endpoint rename in the client and add `compatMode: true` opt-in. Will publish 1.4.1 and post here.

matt: Found logs for `req_abc123` — gateway returned 404 at 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z, backend returned 400 at 14:12:04Z for same request id. That matches mixed-backend rollout.

deploy-bot: staging deploy successful. Prod canary started (5%).

kevin: Patch published as `@redwood/node@1.4.1` and included a short migration note. Support note: the migration renamed `messages` -> `conversation` in 1.4.0, which was a mistake. 1.4.1 restores `messages` compatibility by default.

jordan: Customer confirmed prod calls are green after canary ramped. Closing for now but leaving follow-up to add integration test that simulates mixed-backend rollouts.

kevin: Thanks team — will add test and a release note apologizing for the disruption. :pray:
